rationale: Ownership (unchanged from current discovery, revision fc9ec3b1): the objective communication_kernel_sum_ms is generated exclusively by the 13 fp32 c10d::allreduce_ calls of DDP's final-micro-batch reducer - group f833b57a373d8262a384 (call d0938de87369efd500322679, 12 buckets of 7,087,872 elements = 28,351,488 B each) and group 8525af72c631b94e3dd0 (call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, one 39,385,344-element = 157,541,376 B bucket), 497,759,232 B total on the default NCCL process group; execution_timeline shows exactly 13 NCCL kernels in the step and no other NCCL device work, so no compute-side group can move this metric. The two groups must stay a joint candidate: they share the single c10d.allreduce_.default dispatch target, one site parent (5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0) and one replacement implementation, and communication-ownership.json shows all 13 buckets share member parameter groups, so shared costs cannot be attributed independently. Measured transport facts: collective_calibration (observations/current/collective_calibration-1af5837f.json) puts the warmed intrinsic cost at exactly these sizes at 12x3.536+19.383 = 61.82 ms (rank 0) and 12x3.615+19.522 = 62.90 ms (rank 1), i.e. ~8.0-8.1 GB/s logical payload on the tuner-chosen RING/SIMPLE 2-channel SHM configuration (nccl_tuning-f6198e01.json); the clean baseline (project.json original_baseline) is 63.32/63.67 ms, so only ~0.8 ms (max-rank rank 1) to ~1.5 ms (rank 0) of in-kernel waiting plus one profiled excursion (rank 0 sample 66.48 ms, +4.7 ms over floor) separate the metric from the intrinsic floor - the metric is transfer-bound and the bytes, dtype, DDP bucket configuration and no-comm-hook rules are contract invariants. Concrete failure being repaired (previous-feedback.txt, trial-5a705e709d, decision no_valid_parameter_candidate): the candidate rerouted the bucket allreduces onto a lazily created second NCCL process group with forced NCCL_NCHANNELS/NCCL_PROTO; all three arms (4/Simple, 4/LL128, 16/LL128) blew the step-time constraint (253.9/295.5/289.4 ms vs limit 144.8 ms, because the second PG broke the reducer's comm-stream/compute overlap) and worsened the max-rank kernel sum (89.1/128.4/110.2 ms) through rank-asymmetric in-kernel waiting (rank 1 rose to 87.7-105.3 ms while rank 0 improved to ~60.0 ms), even though exact numerics held (max_abs_error 0.0). Conclusion drawn from that evidence: communicator creation, env-forced channel/protocol tuning and any stream rerouting are excluded levers; the only measured, in-contract headroom left at this site is the launch-skew waiting component, visible as the first-kernel inflation in every profiled sample (execution_timeline-1221e205.json: cross-rank CPU submit spread 10.3-10.7 ms on the first collective with a 14.06 ms first kernel vs 3.6 ms intrinsic; all later kernels sit back-to-back with 1-2 us gaps at intrinsic cost).
hypothesis: A joint functional replacement of both allreduce_ groups that keeps every bucket allreduce on the worker's default NCCL process group by calling the captured reference (context.references) with the original process_group, stream, reduce op and async semantics - explicitly no new_group, no NCCL environment forcing, no comm hook, no bucket reordering, none of the mechanisms the failed trial used - and additionally removes the residual in-kernel launch-skew waiting: on the first allreduce_ call of each reduction burst the replacement performs one bounded cross-rank CPU-side launch alignment (rendezvous on a small gloo/helper group or shared-memory flag, producing no NCCL kernels) so neither rank enters its first ring kernel materially before its peer, then issues the unmodified reference call for all 13 buckets. Because the transfer itself is measured at its intrinsic floor (~62.9 ms max-rank) and is not addressable in-contract, the expected effect is bounded and small: the max-rank median should drop from 63.67 ms toward ~62.9-63.2 ms (about 0.5-0.8 ms, up to ~2.8 ms if skew-excursion samples like the 66.48 ms rank-0 sample are suppressed), with step_ms unchanged or slightly better since the alignment cost moves from counted GPU in-kernel waiting to uncounted CPU rendezvous inside the existing 6.9 ms step-time slack (limit 144.8 vs baseline 137.9 ms). Numerics are untouched: identical fp32 ring SUM on the same communicator in the same order, so exact_gradient_replica_check (atol=0/rtol=0), the global-batch and parameter-update checks behave exactly as baseline, as the failed trial already demonstrated numerically-correct rerouting. Unknowns to test rather than assume: whether the launch-skew component is stable across the 3 profiled samples or dominated by one excursion; whether the alignment rendezvous itself stays below the removed waiting in wall time under the 1.05x step constraint; and whether suppressing skew also stabilizes rank 1's median. Fallback within the same boundary: alignment off after the first bucket, or pure pass-through reference calls, which reduces the candidate to a measured control that empirically pins the transport floor of this 2-channel SHM topology. A null result is informative: it would establish that the objective is at its in-contract floor and that no further site change can move it without violating frozen bytes or DDP invariants.
